**Black Country, New Road** (commonly abbreviated to **BC,NR** or **BCNR**) are an English rock band formed in [Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge "Cambridge") in 2018. Originally founded by Tyler Hyde (bass, vocals), Lewis Evans (vocals, flute, saxophone), [Georgia Ellery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Ellery "Georgia Ellery") (violin, vocals), May Kershaw (vocals, keyboards), Charlie Wayne (drums, backing vocals) and [Isaac Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Wood_(musician) "Isaac Wood (musician)") (guitar, lead vocals), they added their then-seventh member, guitarist Luke Mark, in 2019.

The band gained initial attention through singles "Athens, France" and "[Sunglasses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunglasses_(Black_Country,_New_Road_song) "Sunglasses (Black Country, New Road song)")" in 2019. Their debut album _[For the First Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For\_the\_First\_Time\_(Black\_Country,\_New\_Road\_album) "For the First Time (Black Country, New Road album)")_, released in 2021, received widespread critical acclaim, was nominated for the [Mercury Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Prize "Mercury Prize") and reached No. 4 on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart"). Four days before the release of their 2022 second album _[Ants from Up There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ants\_from\_Up\_There "Ants from Up There")_, Wood left the band, citing mental health struggles. The album received further critical acclaim and commercial success, debuting at No. 3 on the UK Albums Chart.

Following the departure of their lead vocalist Isaac Wood, the band immediately began work on new material, with Hyde, Ellery and Kershaw sharing lead vocal duties. After touring throughout 2022, the band released the [concert film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert_film "Concert film")_[Live at Bush Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_at\_Bush\_Hall "Live at Bush Hall")_, in February 2023, featuring several new compositions and songs that had been written since Wood's departure. In 2025, the band announced their third studio album _[Forever Howlong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forever\_Howlong "Forever Howlong")_, which was released in April 2025.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### 2018–2021: Early career and _For the First Time_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 2018–2021: Early career and For the First Time")]

Main article: [For the First Time (Black Country, New Road album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_the_First_Time_(Black_Country,_New_Road_album) "For the First Time (Black Country, New Road album)")

In 2014, Tyler Hyde, Lewis Evans, Georgia Ellery, May Kershaw, Charlie Wayne, and Isaac Wood formed the [East Cambridgeshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Cambridgeshire "East Cambridgeshire")-based band Nervous Conditions, along with frontman Connor Browne and drummer Jonny Pyke.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1) The group became known for their intense live performances and an eclectic sound.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1) The band had recorded a full-length album in 2017, provisionally titled _Zak's Anniversary;_ however, the album was subsequently shelved and remains officially unreleased.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-2) Following multiple allegations of [sexual assault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_assault "Sexual assault") against Browne, Nervous Conditions split in early 2018.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-4) Browne issued a public apology, and the remaining members—unaware of the accusations at the time—soon formed a new project.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1)

The group, without Browne and Pyke, reconvened soon after as Black Country, New Road in 2018.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1) Formed by graduates of art and music schools,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:11-5) the six-piece was named after [the eponymous road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country_New_Road "Black Country New Road") in the [West Midlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Midlands_(county) "West Midlands (county)") in England,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:1-6) which Wood suggested after using [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia "Wikipedia")'s [random article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Random "Wikipedia:Random") button.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-7) They performed several live shows at the [Brixton Windmill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Windmill,_Brixton "The Windmill, Brixton") venue and gained a small level of notoriety within the [South London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_London "South London") music scene.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-paste-8) According to drummer Charlie Wayne, the band first performed with [Black Midi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Midi "Black Midi") in October 2017, before Black Country, New Road had officially formed.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Smith-2021-9) Although the new band shared much of Nervous Conditions' personnel, their musical direction was distinct from previous efforts.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1)

[![Image 6: Black Country, New Road performing live on stage in January 2020 under colourful lighting, with all seven band members playing instruments like guitars, drums, a violin, a saxophone and a keyboard.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Black_Country%2C_New_Road_%2849387468462%29.jpg/250px-Black_Country%2C_New_Road_%2849387468462%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Black_Country,_New_Road_(49387468462).jpg)

Black Country, New Road performing in January 2020

Their debut single, "Athens, France", was released on 18 January 2019 through the independent label Speedy Wunderground.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-10) In early 2019, Luke Mark joined Black Country, New Road as a second guitarist, expanding the band to a seven-piece lineup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1) This was followed with "[Sunglasses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunglasses_(Black_Country,_New_Road_song) "Sunglasses (Black Country, New Road song)")", the band's second single, released on 26 July 2019.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:8-11) Both releases garnered attention from critics, for experimenting and blending of a variety of sounds,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-cos-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmeinterview-13) and developed a strong [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:11-5) with physical copies reportedly being resold for over [£](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_sterling "Pound sterling")100.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-exclaim-14) Peter Helman of _[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")_ noted the wide variety of genre influences on the track, describing it as a "wild ride",[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:8-11) John Doran of _[The Quietus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Quietus "The Quietus")_ described the band, following the release of "Sunglasses", as "the best in the entire world".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1)

On October 2020, Black Country, New Road signed to [Ninja Tune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninja_Tune "Ninja Tune").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-15) Later that month, on the 28th, the band announced their debut album, _[For the First Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For\_the\_First\_Time\_(Black\_Country,\_New\_Road\_album) "For the First Time (Black Country, New Road album)")_, which was released on 5 February 2021 through Ninja Tune,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nme1-16) alongside the release of its [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single"), "Science Fair".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-cos-12) On 11 January 2021, "Track X" was released as the second single from the album.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-17) The album was produced by Andy Savours and recorded in March 2020 during the early stages of [the first UK COVID-19 lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_lockdown_in_the_United_Kingdom "COVID-19 lockdown in the United Kingdom").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-pitchfork-18) Following the album's release, it was met with critical acclaim[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-19) and charted at number four on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart"), and it became their first number-one release on the [UK Independent Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Independent_Albums_Chart "UK Independent Albums Chart").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-UK-Albums2-20) Their growing popularity led to bookings at major music festivals such as [Glastonbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glastonbury_Festival "Glastonbury Festival"), [Primavera Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primavera_Sound "Primavera Sound"), and [South by Southwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_by_Southwest "South by Southwest") in 2020, although these appearances were cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-exclaim-14)

### 2021–2022: _Ants from Up There_ and Isaac Wood's departure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2021–2022: Ants from Up There and Isaac Wood's departure")]

Main article: [Ants from Up There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ants_from_Up_There "Ants from Up There")

On 12 October 2021, the band announced their second album _[Ants from Up There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ants\_from\_Up\_There "Ants from Up There")_ and released its lead single "Chaos Space Marine".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:4-21) Four of the album's songs were released as singles: "Chaos Space Marine", "Bread Song" on 2 November 2021,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-pfbs-22) "Concorde" on 30 November 2021[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-23) and "Snow Globes" on 19 January 2022.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-24) On 3 November 2021, Black Country, New Road cancelled their upcoming European tour due to a band member's illness.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-25) The band released the _Never Again_ EP on 3 December, a [Rough Trade Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rough_Trade_Records "Rough Trade Records") exclusive limited to 1,500 copies which features covers of songs by [MGMT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MGMT "MGMT"), [ABBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABBA "ABBA") and [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-neveragainLOBF-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-27)

On 31 January 2022, lead vocalist and guitarist Isaac Wood announced his sudden departure from the band four days before the release of _Ants From Up There_ via social media, citing struggles with his mental health.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Pareles-29) This resulted in the cancelling of the band's planned first US tour.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-30) Black Country, New Road announced that the remaining six members had already begun to work on new music without Wood, as they were aware of Wood's planned exit long before it was announced.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-IsaacDeparturePitchfork-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:0-32) Out of respect for Wood, the band has chosen not to perform material from their first two albums live, but has expressed openness to his potential return in the future if he wishes to rejoin.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:0-32) Prior to Wood's departure, Hyde noted that the band's next release might not take the form of a studio album: "I know it's not going to be an album in its normal form. It would be cool to work with an orchestra; it would be cool to do a film score. These are just some of the ideas we're bouncing around at the moment".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-UncutPrintInterview-33) The idea of other band members taking on vocal duties had already been discussed. According to Hyde, the change "wasn't totally new".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:2-34) Since then, vocal duties within the band were shared among Hyde, Evans, Ellery, and Kershaw.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:2-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:3-35)

_Ants from Up There_ was released on 4 February 2022 to universal critical acclaim.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Metacritic-36) It also debuted at number three on the UK Albums Chart, the band's highest placement yet.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-UK-Albums2-20) The band was scheduled to begin a tour in support of the album in February, but the dates were cancelled following Wood's departure.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmeannounce-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-38) A new tour, without Wood, commenced in May and ran through September.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmea2-39) During this period, the band once again road-tested new material.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmea2-39) A deluxe edition of the album was released on 10 June, featuring songs recorded live at the [Queen Elizabeth Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_Hall "Queen Elizabeth Hall").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-40)

### 2022–2024: Transition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2022–2024: Transition")]

Main article: [Live at Bush Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_at_Bush_Hall "Live at Bush Hall")

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Black_Country%2C_New_Road_in_June_2023.jpg/250px-Black_Country%2C_New_Road_in_June_2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Black_Country,_New_Road_in_June_2023.jpg)

Black Country, New Road performing at Glastonbury Festival in June 2023

With Wood no longer a member, the band scheduled and announced a European tour in summer 2022, as well as an American tour supporting Black Midi.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmea2-39)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-41) The band performed new, unreleased songs throughout their 2022 concerts, which Lewis Evans said was written specifically to give the band material to tour with and may not appear on the upcoming third album.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-42) On 14 November 2022, the band released a second EP of covers titled _Never Again Pt. 2_, to celebrate the band's placement on Rough Trade's album of the year list. The EP was limited to 1,500 copies and features covers of songs by [Regina Spektor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regina_Spektor "Regina Spektor"), [Caroline Polachek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caroline_Polachek "Caroline Polachek"), [The Magnetic Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Magnetic_Fields "The Magnetic Fields"), and [Billie Eilish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Eilish "Billie Eilish").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-43)

On 14 February 2023, the band posted a video on social media containing a teaser for something "coming soon" for release on 20 February.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:6-44) It was then announced to be _[Live at Bush Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_at\_Bush\_Hall "Live at Bush Hall")_, a recording of their performances at [Bush Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_Hall "Bush Hall"), London.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-45) The video was recorded over two days[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-46) and was composed entirely of unreleased material that the band had debuted at concerts in 2022, and marks the band's first release of new music since Wood's departure.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-47) An album of the performance was released by the band on 24 March 2023.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-48) On 26 September 2023, it was announced that the band had signed a global publishing deal with [Transgressive Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgressive_Records "Transgressive Records"). Alongside this, it was revealed that the band were working on a follow-up release to _Ants from Up There_ while touring.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-49)

### 2025–present: _Forever Howlong_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2025–present: Forever Howlong")]

Main article: [Forever Howlong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forever_Howlong "Forever Howlong")

On 13 January 2025, the band released a 19-second teaser which included a new logo onto various social media platforms. On 22 January, the band announced that a new single titled "Besties" was set to be released on 30 January.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:7-50) The band later announced the release of their third album _[Forever Howlong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forever\_Howlong "Forever Howlong")_, due to be released on 4 April 2025, accompanied by a North American and European tour.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-51) The second single from the album, titled "Happy Birthday", was released on 3 March, alongside an accompanying video directed by Lesley-Anne Rose.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-52) Their third single from the album, titled "For the Cold Country" was released on 26 March.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-53)

_Forever Howlong_ was released on multiple formats including on [2xLP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonograph_record "Phonograph record"), [CD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compact_disc "Compact disc") and [cassette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compact_cassette "Compact cassette"),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-fhvariants-54) with various collector's editions offering alternate artwork and tracklists.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-fhvariants-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-55) To promote the album, the band embarked on an international tour beginning on 7 April 2025 in [Stockport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockport "Stockport"),[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-56) with performances scheduled through 31 October.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-57)_Forever Howlong_ was released to critical acclaim.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-58) It debuted at number three on the UK Albums Chart and number one on the UK Independent Albums Chart.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-UK-Albums2-20) The album also charted internationally, reaching number 16 in Germany,[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Germany-59) 22 in Australia,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:05-60) and 135 on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), marking their first appearance on that chart.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-BillBoardTAS-61)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Artistry")]

Black Country, New Road's musical style has been described as [experimental rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_rock "Experimental rock"),[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-bpm-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-NME2-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Dempsey-2021-64)[post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk")[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-stereogum-65)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:3-35) and [post-rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-rock "Post-rock").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-stereogum-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-uncut-66) Their music is characterised by a fusion of diverse genres and compositional approaches.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Jenkins-2021-67) While rooted in the dissonant intensity and angular rhythms of post-punk, the band incorporates a wide array of influences that set them apart from more conventional rock acts.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Pareles-29) Their early sound was frequently compared to 1990s experimental rock groups such as [Slint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slint "Slint").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-68) It has also been described as "genre-scrambling"[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Pareles-29) and "deconstructed rock canvas".[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-popmattersafut-69)

Black Country, New Road have also incorporated stylistic elements from [klezmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klezmer "Klezmer"), British [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music"), [progressive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_rock "Progressive rock"), and [minimal music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimal_music "Minimal music").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Pareles-29) Early in their career, the band were described as a centerpiece of a new scene of British rock bands rooted in experimental post-punk with _[Sprechgesang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprechgesang "Sprechgesang")_ – or "talk-singing" – vocals, alongside contemporaries Black Midi, [Squid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band) "Squid (band)"), [Dry Cleaning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_Cleaning_(band) "Dry Cleaning (band)"), [Shame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shame_(band) "Shame (band)"), [Yard Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yard_Act "Yard Act") and Irish band [Fontaines D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontaines_D.C. "Fontaines D.C.")[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Perpetua-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-71) They are considered to be part of the emerging wave of [British rock music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_rock_music "British rock music") known as the [Windmill scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windmill_scene "Windmill scene").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-72)

The band's debut album _For the First Time_ is rooted in [experimental rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_rock "Experimental rock"), [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk"), and [post-rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-rock "Post-rock").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Dempsey-2021-64) Their instrumentation also draws from American composer [Steve Reich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Reich "Steve Reich") and jazz musician [Ornette Coleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornette_Coleman "Ornette Coleman").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:1-6) Wood's vocals were compared to Slint frontman Brian McMahan and [The Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fall_(band) "The Fall (band)") lead singer [Mark E. Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_E._Smith "Mark E. Smith");[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nme.com-73) his lyrics were influenced by American singer-songwriter [Father John Misty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Father_John_Misty "Father John Misty"), with Wood declaring "he's not the best lyricist in the world, but what he is is entirely, entirely honest".[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-74) The band often references other musicians in their songs, such as being associated to "the world's second-best [Slint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slint "Slint") tribute act" in the song "Science Fair".[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-75) "Track X" references their company with Black Midi.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-76) They mention [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West") in their song "Sunglasses" with the line "leave Kanye out of this".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-77) "Athens, France" contains lyrics from [Phoebe Bridgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoebe_Bridgers "Phoebe Bridgers")' "[Motion Sickness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_Sickness_(Phoebe_Bridgers_song) "Motion Sickness (Phoebe Bridgers song)")";[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-78) the original single also references [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande")'s "[Thank U, Next](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank_U,_Next_(song) "Thank U, Next (song)")".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-79) The band has also been noted for their unconventional merchandising choices and [music videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") incorporating surreal stock imagery.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-exclaim-14)

Their second album _Ants From Up There_ was written to feature a more accessible sound.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nme.com-73) It has been described as post-rock, [chamber pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamber_pop "Chamber pop")[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-TLOBF_review-80) and [indie rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_rock "Indie rock").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nme2-81) The band became "obsessed" with Canadian indie rock band [Arcade Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcade_Fire "Arcade Fire") during the United Kingdom's [COVID-19 lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_Kingdom "COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom"); several critics have compared songs such as "Chaos Space Marine" and "The Place Where He Inserted the Blade" to Arcade Fire.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:03-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-84) Black Country, New Road also recalled listening to [Kurt Vile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Vile "Kurt Vile") and [Frank Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Ocean "Frank Ocean") for inspiration during the writing process.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:5-85) With their third album, following the departure of Wood, _Forever Howlong_ has signaled a stylistic shift away from their first two albums, with the band going out of their way to avoid being "melodramatic" and aiming to be more "subtle" within their songwriting.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:3-35) Following Wood's departure, vocal performances across _Forever Howlong_ were taken up by Hyde, Ellery, and Kershaw.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:3-35) The album, in a [press release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_release "Press release"), has been described as [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music"), [progressive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_rock "Progressive rock"), [baroque pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque_pop "Baroque pop") and [alternative rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_rock "Alternative rock"), with comparisons to artists such as [Joanna Newsom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_Newsom "Joanna Newsom"), [Randy Newman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Newman "Randy Newman"), and [Fiona Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiona_Apple "Fiona Apple").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-fhvariants-54) The band also recounted that they avoided utilising instrumentation that they felt was typical for them during the recording process, with Mark stating "there's a lot of different kinds of songs on the album that I don't think we could've done before, but we can now".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:3-35)

## Other projects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Other projects")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Jockstrap_10_23_23_Terminal_West_2_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Jockstrap_10_23_23_Terminal_West_2_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jockstrap_10_23_23_Terminal_West_2_(cropped).jpg)

[Jockstrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jockstrap_(band) "Jockstrap (band)") performing in 2023.

Beyond their own work, the band regularly performed live with fellow London experimental rock group [Black Midi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Midi "Black Midi"), touring collectively as Black Midi, New Road. [Geordie Greep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geordie_Greep "Geordie Greep"), the guitarist and vocalist of Black Midi, said the following: "If there's another band who are really good in the same city, who you also really get on with, there's no reason not to get together and do something proper. It's just making sure you don't do it for the sake of it and you have a solid reason for doing it".[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-86) In June 2021, the group also worked with London musician Ethan P. Flynn, releasing a live version of his song "Television Show".[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-87)

Violinist [Georgia Ellery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Ellery "Georgia Ellery") is one half of the experimental electronic duo [Jockstrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jockstrap_(band) "Jockstrap (band)") with Taylor Skye, who have released two EPs and an album.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-88) She also collaborated with [Jamie xx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_xx "Jamie xx") on a [BBC Radio 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_3 "BBC Radio 3") session on 30 May 2020.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-89) She made her acting debut in 2019's _[Bait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bait\_(2019\_film) "Bait (2019 film)")_,[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:9-90) which won a [British Academy Film award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards") for [Outstanding Debut by a British Writer, Director or Producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Outstanding_Debut_by_a_British_Writer,_Director_or_Producer "BAFTA Award for Outstanding Debut by a British Writer, Director or Producer").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-91) Ellery has performed and recorded as a member of conservatory folk trio Contours and Happy Beigel Klezmer Orkester, a six-piece Klezmer band formed during studies at [Guildhall School of Music and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guildhall_School_of_Music_and_Drama "Guildhall School of Music and Drama").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:9-90)

Bassist Tyler Hyde is the daughter of [Underworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underworld_(band) "Underworld (band)") founder [Karl Hyde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Hyde "Karl Hyde").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmeinterview-13) She released her first music outside of Black Country, New Road under the alias Tyler Cryde, performing a duet with boyfriend Skydaddy on the single "Tear Gas".[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-92) Drummer Charlie Wayne was also a drummer of another British band, [Ugly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugly_(UK_band) "Ugly (UK band)").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-93) Saxophonist Lewis Evans has made a self-titled album under the alias Good with Parents and featured on the [TRAAMS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TRAAMS "TRAAMS") single "The Greyhound".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-94) Evans also contributed saxophone to [Squid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band) "Squid (band)")'s debut album _[Bright Green Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bright\_Green\_Field "Bright Green Field")_, released on 7 May 2021.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-95) Former vocalist Isaac Wood has occasionally released music under his solo moniker The Guest, including an acoustic version of "Track X" called "Track X (The Guest)", performed solo by Wood and predating the formation of Black Country, New Road.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-96)

**Black Country, New Road** (commonly abbreviated to **BC,NR** or **BCNR**) are an English rock band formed in [Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge "Cambridge") in 2018. Originally founded by Tyler Hyde (bass, vocals), Lewis Evans (vocals, flute, saxophone), [Georgia Ellery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Ellery "Georgia Ellery") (violin, vocals), May Kershaw (vocals, keyboards), Charlie Wayne (drums, backing vocals) and [Isaac Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Wood_(musician) "Isaac Wood (musician)") (guitar, lead vocals), they added their then-seventh member, guitarist Luke Mark, in 2019.

The band gained initial attention through singles "Athens, France" and "[Sunglasses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunglasses_(Black_Country,_New_Road_song) "Sunglasses (Black Country, New Road song)")" in 2019. Their debut album _[For the First Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For\_the\_First\_Time\_(Black\_Country,\_New\_Road\_album) "For the First Time (Black Country, New Road album)")_, released in 2021, received widespread critical acclaim, was nominated for the [Mercury Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Prize "Mercury Prize") and reached No. 4 on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart"). Four days before the release of their 2022 second album _[Ants from Up There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ants\_from\_Up\_There "Ants from Up There")_, Wood left the band, citing mental health struggles. The album received further critical acclaim and commercial success, debuting at No. 3 on the UK Albums Chart.

Following the departure of their lead vocalist Isaac Wood, the band immediately began work on new material, with Hyde, Ellery and Kershaw sharing lead vocal duties. After touring throughout 2022, the band released the [concert film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert_film "Concert film")_[Live at Bush Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_at\_Bush\_Hall "Live at Bush Hall")_, in February 2023, featuring several new compositions and songs that had been written since Wood's departure. In 2025, the band announced their third studio album _[Forever Howlong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forever\_Howlong "Forever Howlong")_, which was released in April 2025.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### 2018–2021: Early career and _For the First Time_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 2018–2021: Early career and For the First Time")]

Main article: [For the First Time (Black Country, New Road album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_the_First_Time_(Black_Country,_New_Road_album) "For the First Time (Black Country, New Road album)")

In 2014, Tyler Hyde, Lewis Evans, Georgia Ellery, May Kershaw, Charlie Wayne, and Isaac Wood formed the [East Cambridgeshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Cambridgeshire "East Cambridgeshire")-based band Nervous Conditions, along with frontman Connor Browne and drummer Jonny Pyke.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1) The group became known for their intense live performances and an eclectic sound.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1) The band had recorded a full-length album in 2017, provisionally titled _Zak's Anniversary;_ however, the album was subsequently shelved and remains officially unreleased.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-2) Following multiple allegations of [sexual assault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_assault "Sexual assault") against Browne, Nervous Conditions split in early 2018.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-4) Browne issued a public apology, and the remaining members—unaware of the accusations at the time—soon formed a new project.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1)

The group, without Browne and Pyke, reconvened soon after as Black Country, New Road in 2018.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1) Formed by graduates of art and music schools,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:11-5) the six-piece was named after [the eponymous road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country_New_Road "Black Country New Road") in the [West Midlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Midlands_(county) "West Midlands (county)") in England,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:1-6) which Wood suggested after using [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia "Wikipedia")'s [random article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Random "Wikipedia:Random") button.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-7) They performed several live shows at the [Brixton Windmill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Windmill,_Brixton "The Windmill, Brixton") venue and gained a small level of notoriety within the [South London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_London "South London") music scene.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-paste-8) According to drummer Charlie Wayne, the band first performed with [Black Midi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Midi "Black Midi") in October 2017, before Black Country, New Road had officially formed.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Smith-2021-9) Although the new band shared much of Nervous Conditions' personnel, their musical direction was distinct from previous efforts.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1)

[![Image 6: Black Country, New Road performing live on stage in January 2020 under colourful lighting, with all seven band members playing instruments like guitars, drums, a violin, a saxophone and a keyboard.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Black_Country%2C_New_Road_%2849387468462%29.jpg/250px-Black_Country%2C_New_Road_%2849387468462%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Black_Country,_New_Road_(49387468462).jpg)

Black Country, New Road performing in January 2020

Their debut single, "Athens, France", was released on 18 January 2019 through the independent label Speedy Wunderground.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-10) In early 2019, Luke Mark joined Black Country, New Road as a second guitarist, expanding the band to a seven-piece lineup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1) This was followed with "[Sunglasses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunglasses_(Black_Country,_New_Road_song) "Sunglasses (Black Country, New Road song)")", the band's second single, released on 26 July 2019.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:8-11) Both releases garnered attention from critics, for experimenting and blending of a variety of sounds,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-cos-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmeinterview-13) and developed a strong [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:11-5) with physical copies reportedly being resold for over [£](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_sterling "Pound sterling")100.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-exclaim-14) Peter Helman of _[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")_ noted the wide variety of genre influences on the track, describing it as a "wild ride",[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:8-11) John Doran of _[The Quietus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Quietus "The Quietus")_ described the band, following the release of "Sunglasses", as "the best in the entire world".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:10-1)

On October 2020, Black Country, New Road signed to [Ninja Tune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninja_Tune "Ninja Tune").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-15) Later that month, on the 28th, the band announced their debut album, _[For the First Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For\_the\_First\_Time\_(Black\_Country,\_New\_Road\_album) "For the First Time (Black Country, New Road album)")_, which was released on 5 February 2021 through Ninja Tune,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nme1-16) alongside the release of its [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single"), "Science Fair".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-cos-12) On 11 January 2021, "Track X" was released as the second single from the album.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-17) The album was produced by Andy Savours and recorded in March 2020 during the early stages of [the first UK COVID-19 lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_lockdown_in_the_United_Kingdom "COVID-19 lockdown in the United Kingdom").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-pitchfork-18) Following the album's release, it was met with critical acclaim[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-19) and charted at number four on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart"), and it became their first number-one release on the [UK Independent Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Independent_Albums_Chart "UK Independent Albums Chart").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-UK-Albums2-20) Their growing popularity led to bookings at major music festivals such as [Glastonbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glastonbury_Festival "Glastonbury Festival"), [Primavera Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primavera_Sound "Primavera Sound"), and [South by Southwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_by_Southwest "South by Southwest") in 2020, although these appearances were cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-exclaim-14)

### 2021–2022: _Ants from Up There_ and Isaac Wood's departure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2021–2022: Ants from Up There and Isaac Wood's departure")]

Main article: [Ants from Up There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ants_from_Up_There "Ants from Up There")

On 12 October 2021, the band announced their second album _[Ants from Up There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ants\_from\_Up\_There "Ants from Up There")_ and released its lead single "Chaos Space Marine".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:4-21) Four of the album's songs were released as singles: "Chaos Space Marine", "Bread Song" on 2 November 2021,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-pfbs-22) "Concorde" on 30 November 2021[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-23) and "Snow Globes" on 19 January 2022.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-24) On 3 November 2021, Black Country, New Road cancelled their upcoming European tour due to a band member's illness.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-25) The band released the _Never Again_ EP on 3 December, a [Rough Trade Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rough_Trade_Records "Rough Trade Records") exclusive limited to 1,500 copies which features covers of songs by [MGMT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MGMT "MGMT"), [ABBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABBA "ABBA") and [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-neveragainLOBF-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-27)

On 31 January 2022, lead vocalist and guitarist Isaac Wood announced his sudden departure from the band four days before the release of _Ants From Up There_ via social media, citing struggles with his mental health.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Pareles-29) This resulted in the cancelling of the band's planned first US tour.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-30) Black Country, New Road announced that the remaining six members had already begun to work on new music without Wood, as they were aware of Wood's planned exit long before it was announced.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-IsaacDeparturePitchfork-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:0-32) Out of respect for Wood, the band has chosen not to perform material from their first two albums live, but has expressed openness to his potential return in the future if he wishes to rejoin.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:0-32) Prior to Wood's departure, Hyde noted that the band's next release might not take the form of a studio album: "I know it's not going to be an album in its normal form. It would be cool to work with an orchestra; it would be cool to do a film score. These are just some of the ideas we're bouncing around at the moment".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-UncutPrintInterview-33) The idea of other band members taking on vocal duties had already been discussed. According to Hyde, the change "wasn't totally new".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:2-34) Since then, vocal duties within the band were shared among Hyde, Evans, Ellery, and Kershaw.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:2-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:3-35)

_Ants from Up There_ was released on 4 February 2022 to universal critical acclaim.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Metacritic-36) It also debuted at number three on the UK Albums Chart, the band's highest placement yet.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-UK-Albums2-20) The band was scheduled to begin a tour in support of the album in February, but the dates were cancelled following Wood's departure.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmeannounce-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-38) A new tour, without Wood, commenced in May and ran through September.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmea2-39) During this period, the band once again road-tested new material.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmea2-39) A deluxe edition of the album was released on 10 June, featuring songs recorded live at the [Queen Elizabeth Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_Hall "Queen Elizabeth Hall").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-40)

### 2022–2024: Transition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2022–2024: Transition")]

Main article: [Live at Bush Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_at_Bush_Hall "Live at Bush Hall")

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Black_Country%2C_New_Road_in_June_2023.jpg/250px-Black_Country%2C_New_Road_in_June_2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Black_Country,_New_Road_in_June_2023.jpg)

Black Country, New Road performing at Glastonbury Festival in June 2023

With Wood no longer a member, the band scheduled and announced a European tour in summer 2022, as well as an American tour supporting Black Midi.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmea2-39)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-41) The band performed new, unreleased songs throughout their 2022 concerts, which Lewis Evans said was written specifically to give the band material to tour with and may not appear on the upcoming third album.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-42) On 14 November 2022, the band released a second EP of covers titled _Never Again Pt. 2_, to celebrate the band's placement on Rough Trade's album of the year list. The EP was limited to 1,500 copies and features covers of songs by [Regina Spektor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regina_Spektor "Regina Spektor"), [Caroline Polachek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caroline_Polachek "Caroline Polachek"), [The Magnetic Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Magnetic_Fields "The Magnetic Fields"), and [Billie Eilish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Eilish "Billie Eilish").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-43)

On 14 February 2023, the band posted a video on social media containing a teaser for something "coming soon" for release on 20 February.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:6-44) It was then announced to be _[Live at Bush Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_at\_Bush\_Hall "Live at Bush Hall")_, a recording of their performances at [Bush Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_Hall "Bush Hall"), London.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-45) The video was recorded over two days[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-46) and was composed entirely of unreleased material that the band had debuted at concerts in 2022, and marks the band's first release of new music since Wood's departure.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-47) An album of the performance was released by the band on 24 March 2023.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-48) On 26 September 2023, it was announced that the band had signed a global publishing deal with [Transgressive Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgressive_Records "Transgressive Records"). Alongside this, it was revealed that the band were working on a follow-up release to _Ants from Up There_ while touring.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-49)

### 2025–present: _Forever Howlong_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2025–present: Forever Howlong")]

Main article: [Forever Howlong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forever_Howlong "Forever Howlong")

On 13 January 2025, the band released a 19-second teaser which included a new logo onto various social media platforms. On 22 January, the band announced that a new single titled "Besties" was set to be released on 30 January.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:7-50) The band later announced the release of their third album _[Forever Howlong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forever\_Howlong "Forever Howlong")_, due to be released on 4 April 2025, accompanied by a North American and European tour.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-51) The second single from the album, titled "Happy Birthday", was released on 3 March, alongside an accompanying video directed by Lesley-Anne Rose.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-52) Their third single from the album, titled "For the Cold Country" was released on 26 March.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-53)

_Forever Howlong_ was released on multiple formats including on [2xLP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonograph_record "Phonograph record"), [CD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compact_disc "Compact disc") and [cassette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compact_cassette "Compact cassette"),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-fhvariants-54) with various collector's editions offering alternate artwork and tracklists.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-fhvariants-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-55) To promote the album, the band embarked on an international tour beginning on 7 April 2025 in [Stockport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockport "Stockport"),[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-56) with performances scheduled through 31 October.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-57)_Forever Howlong_ was released to critical acclaim.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-58) It debuted at number three on the UK Albums Chart and number one on the UK Independent Albums Chart.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-UK-Albums2-20) The album also charted internationally, reaching number 16 in Germany,[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Germany-59) 22 in Australia,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:05-60) and 135 on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), marking their first appearance on that chart.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-BillBoardTAS-61)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Artistry")]

Black Country, New Road's musical style has been described as [experimental rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_rock "Experimental rock"),[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-bpm-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-NME2-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Dempsey-2021-64)[post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk")[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-stereogum-65)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:3-35) and [post-rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-rock "Post-rock").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-stereogum-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-uncut-66) Their music is characterised by a fusion of diverse genres and compositional approaches.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Jenkins-2021-67) While rooted in the dissonant intensity and angular rhythms of post-punk, the band incorporates a wide array of influences that set them apart from more conventional rock acts.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Pareles-29) Their early sound was frequently compared to 1990s experimental rock groups such as [Slint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slint "Slint").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-68) It has also been described as "genre-scrambling"[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Pareles-29) and "deconstructed rock canvas".[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-popmattersafut-69)

Black Country, New Road have also incorporated stylistic elements from [klezmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klezmer "Klezmer"), British [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music"), [progressive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_rock "Progressive rock"), and [minimal music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimal_music "Minimal music").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Pareles-29) Early in their career, the band were described as a centerpiece of a new scene of British rock bands rooted in experimental post-punk with _[Sprechgesang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprechgesang "Sprechgesang")_ – or "talk-singing" – vocals, alongside contemporaries Black Midi, [Squid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band) "Squid (band)"), [Dry Cleaning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_Cleaning_(band) "Dry Cleaning (band)"), [Shame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shame_(band) "Shame (band)"), [Yard Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yard_Act "Yard Act") and Irish band [Fontaines D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontaines_D.C. "Fontaines D.C.")[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Perpetua-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-71) They are considered to be part of the emerging wave of [British rock music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_rock_music "British rock music") known as the [Windmill scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windmill_scene "Windmill scene").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-72)

The band's debut album _For the First Time_ is rooted in [experimental rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_rock "Experimental rock"), [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk"), and [post-rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-rock "Post-rock").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-Dempsey-2021-64) Their instrumentation also draws from American composer [Steve Reich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Reich "Steve Reich") and jazz musician [Ornette Coleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornette_Coleman "Ornette Coleman").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:1-6) Wood's vocals were compared to Slint frontman Brian McMahan and [The Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fall_(band) "The Fall (band)") lead singer [Mark E. Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_E._Smith "Mark E. Smith");[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nme.com-73) his lyrics were influenced by American singer-songwriter [Father John Misty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Father_John_Misty "Father John Misty"), with Wood declaring "he's not the best lyricist in the world, but what he is is entirely, entirely honest".[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-74) The band often references other musicians in their songs, such as being associated to "the world's second-best [Slint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slint "Slint") tribute act" in the song "Science Fair".[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-75) "Track X" references their company with Black Midi.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-76) They mention [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West") in their song "Sunglasses" with the line "leave Kanye out of this".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-77) "Athens, France" contains lyrics from [Phoebe Bridgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoebe_Bridgers "Phoebe Bridgers")' "[Motion Sickness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_Sickness_(Phoebe_Bridgers_song) "Motion Sickness (Phoebe Bridgers song)")";[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-78) the original single also references [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande")'s "[Thank U, Next](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank_U,_Next_(song) "Thank U, Next (song)")".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-79) The band has also been noted for their unconventional merchandising choices and [music videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") incorporating surreal stock imagery.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-exclaim-14)

Their second album _Ants From Up There_ was written to feature a more accessible sound.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nme.com-73) It has been described as post-rock, [chamber pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamber_pop "Chamber pop")[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-TLOBF_review-80) and [indie rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_rock "Indie rock").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nme2-81) The band became "obsessed" with Canadian indie rock band [Arcade Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcade_Fire "Arcade Fire") during the United Kingdom's [COVID-19 lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_Kingdom "COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom"); several critics have compared songs such as "Chaos Space Marine" and "The Place Where He Inserted the Blade" to Arcade Fire.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:03-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-84) Black Country, New Road also recalled listening to [Kurt Vile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Vile "Kurt Vile") and [Frank Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Ocean "Frank Ocean") for inspiration during the writing process.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:5-85) With their third album, following the departure of Wood, _Forever Howlong_ has signaled a stylistic shift away from their first two albums, with the band going out of their way to avoid being "melodramatic" and aiming to be more "subtle" within their songwriting.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:3-35) Following Wood's departure, vocal performances across _Forever Howlong_ were taken up by Hyde, Ellery, and Kershaw.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:3-35) The album, in a [press release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_release "Press release"), has been described as [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music"), [progressive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_rock "Progressive rock"), [baroque pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque_pop "Baroque pop") and [alternative rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_rock "Alternative rock"), with comparisons to artists such as [Joanna Newsom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_Newsom "Joanna Newsom"), [Randy Newman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Newman "Randy Newman"), and [Fiona Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiona_Apple "Fiona Apple").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-fhvariants-54) The band also recounted that they avoided utilising instrumentation that they felt was typical for them during the recording process, with Mark stating "there's a lot of different kinds of songs on the album that I don't think we could've done before, but we can now".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:3-35)

## Other projects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Black_Country,_New_Road&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Other projects")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Jockstrap_10_23_23_Terminal_West_2_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Jockstrap_10_23_23_Terminal_West_2_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jockstrap_10_23_23_Terminal_West_2_(cropped).jpg)

[Jockstrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jockstrap_(band) "Jockstrap (band)") performing in 2023.

Beyond their own work, the band regularly performed live with fellow London experimental rock group [Black Midi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Midi "Black Midi"), touring collectively as Black Midi, New Road. [Geordie Greep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geordie_Greep "Geordie Greep"), the guitarist and vocalist of Black Midi, said the following: "If there's another band who are really good in the same city, who you also really get on with, there's no reason not to get together and do something proper. It's just making sure you don't do it for the sake of it and you have a solid reason for doing it".[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-86) In June 2021, the group also worked with London musician Ethan P. Flynn, releasing a live version of his song "Television Show".[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-87)

Violinist [Georgia Ellery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Ellery "Georgia Ellery") is one half of the experimental electronic duo [Jockstrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jockstrap_(band) "Jockstrap (band)") with Taylor Skye, who have released two EPs and an album.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-88) She also collaborated with [Jamie xx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_xx "Jamie xx") on a [BBC Radio 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_3 "BBC Radio 3") session on 30 May 2020.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-89) She made her acting debut in 2019's _[Bait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bait\_(2019\_film) "Bait (2019 film)")_,[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:9-90) which won a [British Academy Film award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards") for [Outstanding Debut by a British Writer, Director or Producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Outstanding_Debut_by_a_British_Writer,_Director_or_Producer "BAFTA Award for Outstanding Debut by a British Writer, Director or Producer").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-91) Ellery has performed and recorded as a member of conservatory folk trio Contours and Happy Beigel Klezmer Orkester, a six-piece Klezmer band formed during studies at [Guildhall School of Music and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guildhall_School_of_Music_and_Drama "Guildhall School of Music and Drama").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-:9-90)

Bassist Tyler Hyde is the daughter of [Underworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underworld_(band) "Underworld (band)") founder [Karl Hyde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Hyde "Karl Hyde").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-nmeinterview-13) She released her first music outside of Black Country, New Road under the alias Tyler Cryde, performing a duet with boyfriend Skydaddy on the single "Tear Gas".[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-92) Drummer Charlie Wayne was also a drummer of another British band, [Ugly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugly_(UK_band) "Ugly (UK band)").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-93) Saxophonist Lewis Evans has made a self-titled album under the alias Good with Parents and featured on the [TRAAMS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TRAAMS "TRAAMS") single "The Greyhound".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-94) Evans also contributed saxophone to [Squid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band) "Squid (band)")'s debut album _[Bright Green Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bright\_Green\_Field "Bright Green Field")_, released on 7 May 2021.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-95) Former vocalist Isaac Wood has occasionally released music under his solo moniker The Guest, including an acoustic version of "Track X" called "Track X (The Guest)", performed solo by Wood and predating the formation of Black Country, New Road.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road#cite_note-96)
