Musical artist

**Jojo Orme**, known professionally as **Heartworms**, is an English musician.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-FredPerry-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-:0-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Heartworms_(musician)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Josephine Orme[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-3) was born in central [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), England in 1998 or 1999.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-:0-2) She has Afghan and Pakistani heritage on her father's side, and Danish and Chinese on her mother's.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-4) Orme was raised in [Cheltenham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham "Cheltenham"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-dazed1-5) She grew up with the music her mother listened to, including artists such as [Hot Chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Chocolate "Hot Chocolate"), [Fleetwood Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleetwood_Mac "Fleetwood Mac"), [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson"), and [Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_(musician) "Prince (musician)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-rpm-6) She left home at 14 to enter foster care.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-quietus2-7) Orme studied Production and Performance at [South Gloucestershire and Stroud College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Gloucestershire_and_Stroud_College "South Gloucestershire and Stroud College")[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-nme1-8) wanting to become a producer as "there's not many in the industry".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-quietus2-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Heartworms_(musician)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Orme took the name 'Heartworms' from [the Shins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shins "The Shins") 2017 [album of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(album) "Heartworms (album)"). She met producer [Dan Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Carey_(record_producer) "Dan Carey (record producer)") over [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), and he asked her to send him some demos.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-utr1-9) Much of her early career was spent performing at [the Windmill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Windmill,_Brixton "The Windmill, Brixton") venue in Brixton, alongside Black Country, New Road, [Goat Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_Girl "Goat Girl"), [the Last Dinner Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_Dinner_Party "The Last Dinner Party") and [PVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PVA_(band) "PVA (band)").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-11) In 2022, she signed to Carey's [Speedy Wunderground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground "Speedy Wunderground") label, and released the single "Consistent Dedication".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-nme1-8) Her debut EP _A Comforting Notion_ was released in 2023,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-dazed1-5) alongside a limited edition [Airfix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airfix "Airfix")[Spitfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spitfire "Spitfire") model.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-quietus-12) She went on to earn support slots with [the Kills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kills "The Kills") and [St Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Vincent_(musician) "St. Vincent (musician)").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-nme2-13)

In February 2025, Orme's debut album _[Glutton for Punishment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glutton\_for\_Punishment\_(album) "Glutton for Punishment (album)")_ was released to critical acclaim, including a five-star review from _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-nme3-14)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Heartworms_(musician)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Artistry")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Heartworms%2C_Green_Door_Store%2C_Brighton%2C_UK_22_March_2023.jpg/250px-Heartworms%2C_Green_Door_Store%2C_Brighton%2C_UK_22_March_2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Heartworms,_Green_Door_Store,_Brighton,_UK_22_March_2023.jpg)

Orme performing at the Green Door Store, Brighton in 2023

Heartworms' music has been categorised by critics as [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16)[gothic rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_rock "Gothic rock")[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16) and [dance punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_punk "Dance punk").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16) She often incorporates elements of [electroclash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroclash "Electroclash"), [post-industrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-industrial_music "Post-industrial music"), 1990s and 2000s [techno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Techno "Techno") and [electronic dance music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)

She said she "discovered [the Cure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cure "The Cure") and [Siouxsie and the Banshees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouxsie_and_the_Banshees "Siouxsie and the Banshees")" while at [university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University "University") and was attracted to what was musically "dark".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-rpm-6) Her other influences include [PJ Harvey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PJ_Harvey "PJ Harvey") and her album _[To Bring You My Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To\_Bring\_You\_My\_Love "To Bring You My Love")_ (1995),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-rpm-6)[Killing Joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_Joke "Killing Joke")'s _[Killing Joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing\_Joke\_(1980\_album) "Killing Joke (1980 album)")_ (1980), [Grauzone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauzone "Grauzone")'s _Grauzone_ (1981), [the Sisters of Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sisters_of_Mercy "The Sisters of Mercy")'s _[Floodland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floodland\_(album) "Floodland (album)")_ (1987), [Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Cave_and_the_Bad_Seeds "Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds")' _[Push the Sky Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push\_the\_Sky\_Away "Push the Sky Away")_ (2013), [Sóley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%B3ley "Sóley")'s Krómantík (2014), [Nox Arcana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nox_Arcana "Nox Arcana")'s _[Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic\_(Nox\_Arcana\_album) "Gothic (Nox Arcana album)")_ (2015), Drahla's _Useless Coordinates_ (2019),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-17)[Interpol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpol_(band) "Interpol (band)") and [the Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Clash "The Clash") - plus classical music composers like [Frédéric Chopin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%A9d%C3%A9ric_Chopin "Frédéric Chopin").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-18)

Musical artist

**Jojo Orme**, known professionally as **Heartworms**, is an English musician.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-FredPerry-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-:0-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Heartworms_(musician)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Josephine Orme[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-3) was born in central [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), England in 1998 or 1999.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-:0-2) She has Afghan and Pakistani heritage on her father's side, and Danish and Chinese on her mother's.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-4) Orme was raised in [Cheltenham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham "Cheltenham"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-dazed1-5) She grew up with the music her mother listened to, including artists such as [Hot Chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Chocolate "Hot Chocolate"), [Fleetwood Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleetwood_Mac "Fleetwood Mac"), [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson"), and [Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_(musician) "Prince (musician)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-rpm-6) She left home at 14 to enter foster care.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-quietus2-7) Orme studied Production and Performance at [South Gloucestershire and Stroud College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Gloucestershire_and_Stroud_College "South Gloucestershire and Stroud College")[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-nme1-8) wanting to become a producer as "there's not many in the industry".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-quietus2-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Heartworms_(musician)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Orme took the name 'Heartworms' from [the Shins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shins "The Shins") 2017 [album of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(album) "Heartworms (album)"). She met producer [Dan Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Carey_(record_producer) "Dan Carey (record producer)") over [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), and he asked her to send him some demos.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-utr1-9) Much of her early career was spent performing at [the Windmill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Windmill,_Brixton "The Windmill, Brixton") venue in Brixton, alongside Black Country, New Road, [Goat Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_Girl "Goat Girl"), [the Last Dinner Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_Dinner_Party "The Last Dinner Party") and [PVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PVA_(band) "PVA (band)").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-11) In 2022, she signed to Carey's [Speedy Wunderground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground "Speedy Wunderground") label, and released the single "Consistent Dedication".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-nme1-8) Her debut EP _A Comforting Notion_ was released in 2023,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-dazed1-5) alongside a limited edition [Airfix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airfix "Airfix")[Spitfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spitfire "Spitfire") model.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-quietus-12) She went on to earn support slots with [the Kills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kills "The Kills") and [St Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Vincent_(musician) "St. Vincent (musician)").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-nme2-13)

In February 2025, Orme's debut album _[Glutton for Punishment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glutton\_for\_Punishment\_(album) "Glutton for Punishment (album)")_ was released to critical acclaim, including a five-star review from _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-nme3-14)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Heartworms_(musician)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Artistry")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Heartworms%2C_Green_Door_Store%2C_Brighton%2C_UK_22_March_2023.jpg/250px-Heartworms%2C_Green_Door_Store%2C_Brighton%2C_UK_22_March_2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Heartworms,_Green_Door_Store,_Brighton,_UK_22_March_2023.jpg)

Orme performing at the Green Door Store, Brighton in 2023

Heartworms' music has been categorised by critics as [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16)[gothic rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_rock "Gothic rock")[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16) and [dance punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_punk "Dance punk").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16) She often incorporates elements of [electroclash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroclash "Electroclash"), [post-industrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-industrial_music "Post-industrial music"), 1990s and 2000s [techno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Techno "Techno") and [electronic dance music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)

She said she "discovered [the Cure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cure "The Cure") and [Siouxsie and the Banshees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouxsie_and_the_Banshees "Siouxsie and the Banshees")" while at [university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University "University") and was attracted to what was musically "dark".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-rpm-6) Her other influences include [PJ Harvey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PJ_Harvey "PJ Harvey") and her album _[To Bring You My Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To\_Bring\_You\_My\_Love "To Bring You My Love")_ (1995),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-rpm-6)[Killing Joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_Joke "Killing Joke")'s _[Killing Joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing\_Joke\_(1980\_album) "Killing Joke (1980 album)")_ (1980), [Grauzone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauzone "Grauzone")'s _Grauzone_ (1981), [the Sisters of Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sisters_of_Mercy "The Sisters of Mercy")'s _[Floodland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floodland\_(album) "Floodland (album)")_ (1987), [Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Cave_and_the_Bad_Seeds "Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds")' _[Push the Sky Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push\_the\_Sky\_Away "Push the Sky Away")_ (2013), [Sóley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%B3ley "Sóley")'s Krómantík (2014), [Nox Arcana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nox_Arcana "Nox Arcana")'s _[Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic\_(Nox\_Arcana\_album) "Gothic (Nox Arcana album)")_ (2015), Drahla's _Useless Coordinates_ (2019),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-17)[Interpol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpol_(band) "Interpol (band)") and [the Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Clash "The Clash") - plus classical music composers like [Frédéric Chopin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%A9d%C3%A9ric_Chopin "Frédéric Chopin").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(band)#cite_note-18)

**Daniel De Mussenden Carey** (born 24 December 1969)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-1)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable\_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_] is an English record producer, songwriter, mixer and remixer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-bmi-2) He owns his own studio in [South London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_London "South London")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-3) and runs the record label Speedy Wunderground.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-4) His production work for Speedy Wunderground bands such as Black Country, New Road, [Black Midi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Midi "Black Midi"), and [Squid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band) "Squid (band)") was instrumental in the creation of the [Windmill scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windmill_scene "Windmill scene"), also known as the "Speedy scene".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-5)

In 2014, Carey received two [Mercury Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Prize "Mercury Prize") nominations for his production work on two nominated albums: _[Everybody Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody\_Down "Everybody Down")_ by [Kae Tempest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kae_Tempest "Kae Tempest") and _[First Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First\_Mind "First Mind")_ by [Nick Mulvey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Mulvey "Nick Mulvey").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-spy-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-nme-7) In 2019, Carey earned two further Mercury Prize nominations for his production work on the albums _[Schlagenheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlagenheim "Schlagenheim")_ by [Black Midi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Midi "Black Midi") and _[Dogrel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dogrel "Dogrel")_ by [Fontaines D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontaines_D.C. "Fontaines D.C."). He earned a fifth nomination in 2025 for [Jacob Alon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Alon "Jacob Alon")'s _[In Limerence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In\_Limerence "In Limerence")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-8)

Carey produced and played synthesizer on the [self-titled debut album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wet_Leg_(album) "Wet Leg (album)") by the British band [Wet Leg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wet_Leg "Wet Leg"). Carey previously produced for the London-based labels Dust Records, Dust2Dust and DMI. He was also one half of the group Danmass, which released music on all three labels and [Skint Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skint_Records "Skint Records"). Danmass released one album, _Formfreaks_, on Dust2Dust in 1999.

**Daniel De Mussenden Carey** (born 24 December 1969)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-1)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable\_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_] is an English record producer, songwriter, mixer and remixer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-bmi-2) He owns his own studio in [South London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_London "South London")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-3) and runs the record label Speedy Wunderground.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-4) His production work for Speedy Wunderground bands such as Black Country, New Road, [Black Midi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Midi "Black Midi"), and [Squid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band) "Squid (band)") was instrumental in the creation of the [Windmill scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windmill_scene "Windmill scene"), also known as the "Speedy scene".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-5)

In 2014, Carey received two [Mercury Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Prize "Mercury Prize") nominations for his production work on two nominated albums: _[Everybody Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody\_Down "Everybody Down")_ by [Kae Tempest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kae_Tempest "Kae Tempest") and _[First Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First\_Mind "First Mind")_ by [Nick Mulvey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Mulvey "Nick Mulvey").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-spy-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-nme-7) In 2019, Carey earned two further Mercury Prize nominations for his production work on the albums _[Schlagenheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlagenheim "Schlagenheim")_ by [Black Midi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Midi "Black Midi") and _[Dogrel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dogrel "Dogrel")_ by [Fontaines D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontaines_D.C. "Fontaines D.C."). He earned a fifth nomination in 2025 for [Jacob Alon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Alon "Jacob Alon")'s _[In Limerence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In\_Limerence "In Limerence")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground#cite_note-8)

Carey produced and played synthesizer on the [self-titled debut album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wet_Leg_(album) "Wet Leg (album)") by the British band [Wet Leg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wet_Leg "Wet Leg"). Carey previously produced for the London-based labels Dust Records, Dust2Dust and DMI. He was also one half of the group Danmass, which released music on all three labels and [Skint Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skint_Records "Skint Records"). Danmass released one album, _Formfreaks_, on Dust2Dust in 1999.
